title: Fruit and Vegetable Products - Determination of Titratable Acidity
clause_1_scope: This Indian Standard (IS 13844) covers Fruit and Vegetable Products - Determination of Titratable Acidity. This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) which is identical with ISO 750 : 1998 'Fruit and vegetable products — Determination of titratable acidity' issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( ISO ) was adopted by the Processed Fruit and Vegetable Products Sectional Committee and approval of the Food and Agriculture Division Council. This standard was originally published in 1 993 based on the earlier version of the International Standard, namely, ISO 750 : 1981 under dual numbering. This is being revised to align with the revised version, namely, ISO 750 : 1998. In the adopted standard certain terminology and conventions are not identical to those used in the Indian Standards. Attention is particularly drawn to the following: a) Wherever the words 'International Standard' appear referring to this standard, they should be read as 'Indian Standard'; and b) Comma ( , ) has been used as a decimal marker while in Indian Standards, the current practice is to use a point (
clause_3_terminology: Fruit and Vegetable Products - Determination of Titratable Acidity

marking_requirements: Each container, package or piece shall be marked indelibly with the manufacturer's name, brand/trademark, grade, batch number, and month/year of manufacture.
The product may also be marked with the Standard Mark (BIS Certification Mark) governed by the Bureau of Indian Standards Act.
